Messages.Author: Trigger
Messages.Body:
Curious if Tupdog's ability (underlined) supersedes his Tremere antitribu slave requirement of not being able to perform  actions if the Tremere antitribue is not ready?

Tupdog, 1, POT VIS, Gargoyle, 3, [LoB:C]

Sabbat. Tremere antitribu slave: Visceratika cards cost Tupdog 1 less blood to play. Tupdog may enter combat with any minion as a  action. Tupdogs are not unique. At the end of your minion phase, burn Tupdog and move the top card from your crypt to your uncontrolled region. Flight.

Messages.Author: extrala
Messages.Body: The tupdog cannot take  actions unless a Tremere antitribu is ready. This includes his built in  action.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Blooded wrote:
> Apart from it would be imbalanced, no-one has ever to my satisfaction explained to me why 1.4 does not over ride his slave status
>
Tupdog's card text provides an additional  action that he can take, when he can take a  action - much like a cardless bleed action, a cardless diablerie action, the  action to mess with Powerbase: Chicago, or Bum's Rush. When Tupdog is able to take a  action, he can pick from any of those actions - including the extra one from his card text.

Until he has a master vampire out, however, he can't take a  action at all.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> jamesatzephyr wrote:
>
> > Blooded wrote:
> > Apart from it would be imbalanced, no-one has ever to my satisfaction explained to me why 1.4 does not over ride his slave status
> >
> Tupdog's card text provides an additional  action that he can take, when he can take a  action - much like a cardless bleed action, a cardless diablerie action, the  action to mess with Powerbase: Chicago, or Bum's Rush. When Tupdog is able to take a  action, he can pick from any of those actions - including the extra one from his card text.
>
> Until he has a master vampire out, however, he can't take a  action at all.
>
Correct. When a effect overrides a rule, it doesn't extend beyond the scope of that effect.

"Tupdog may enter combat with any minion as a  action" isn't the same as "Tupdog may enter combat with any minion as a  action and can take  actions ignoring its slave status".

So basically,
1/ he can enter combat as a  action
2/ he can't take  actions while there isn't a ready !Tremere.

As always, the "can't" part take precedence over the "can" part.
Here's another example for this: Tupdog can enter combat with A + A has a Secure Haven (can't take  actions against him) = Tupdog can't enter combat with A.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Ankha wrote:
> Correct. When a effect overrides a rule, it doesn't extend beyond the scope of that effect.
>
This is also true for Walker Grimes: "Master cards that target Walker cost you an additional pool."
Since only the player who plays a card pays the cost of it (unless explicit card text such as a Ravnos Cache), the controller of Walker doesn't pay when other players play a master card on him. "cost you" is the key part. Walker's effect doesn't allow players to pay cards played by other players.
